To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a relativistic equation of state that is flexible enough for use in hadronic transport simulations and that reproduces thermodynamical behavior of dense hadronic matter, including critical behavior.

we developed a flexible, relativistic density functional parameterization that is suited for use in computationally expensive hadronic transport simulations, that we implemented it in a hadronic transport code, and that we used this to study phase transitions in hadronic systems.

1) hadronic transport can successfully be used to study the bulk properties of dense nuclear matter, and 2) hadronic transport simulations show that the second order cumulants of two-particle correlation functions are sensitive to the phase diagram of nuclear matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of dense nuclear matter and its phase diagram, in particular with a focus on critical behavior.
the study of the phase diagram of QCD matter at finite temperature and density, with a particular focus on the critical point.
the development of a relativistic density-functional equation of state suited to hadronic transport simulations, and the study of the phase structure of dense matter using such simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hadronic transport model SMASH, with the relativistic density functional parameterization of the equation of state, is able to reproduce the thermodynamic behavior of the equation of sate and can therefore be used to study the critical behavior of dense nuclear matter.

the SMASH transport model is able to reproduce the expected behavior of a relativistic equation of state in a transport simulation, and that the transport model is a suitable tool for studying the QCD phase diagram at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential.

the hadronic transport model SMASH, when coupled to the equation of state presented here, can be used to simulate the evolution of a hot and dense hadronic system and study the critical behavior of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of hadronic transport to study critical phenomena in dense nuclear matter.

we have demonstrated that relativistic hadronic transport simulations with a relativistic equation of state can be used to explore the thermodynamic and dynamic behavior in the vicinity of the QCD critical point.

the hadronic transport approach can be used to simulate critical phenomena in hadronic matter, and that the second order cumulants are a promising observable for experimental studies of critical behavior in heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hadronic transport is a promising tool for the study of critical phenomena and the search for the critical point in heavy-ion collisions.
hadronic transport simulations can be used to explore the QCD phase diagram in a controlled way.

relativistic hadronic transport simulations can be used to investigate the phase diagram of dense hadronic matter and its critical behavior, and that this can be done with the same level of detail and precision as in heavy-ion collision experiments, but with the additional flexibility of being able to study the critical behavior in systems of different size and composition.
